replies.body: Done in 5a3ec52e. Streamed and non-streamed `create` now derive finish reasons from the status on both model and agent spans, regardless of content capture, and the explicit block in `_CreateStreamMixin._record_interaction` is gone. `in_progress` or a missing status gives no finish reason. Before this, a non-streamed model span with content capture on reported `stop` even for `in_progress`.

threads.body:
The rebuild-from-steps path is only covered by a plain-text cassette. The other new streaming tests use hand-built `MagicMock` events, which don't match the SDK's real event types, so a wrong field name wouldn't fail them. Also, streamed `create` still has no tests for a mid-stream error, a caller-side error, or close/early-close, and this PR changes how those finish.

What do you think about following the OpenAI/Anthropic pattern?

- Record a streamed tool-call cassette (sync + async) that ends in `requires_action`, and check the rebuilt `tool_call` part and `finish_reasons == ("tool_calls",)` with content capture on and off.
- Inject failures on top of a recorded cassette by wrapping the SDK stream in a delegate that raises after N events, like [`ErrorInjectingStreamDelegate`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python-genai/blob/main/instrumentation/opentelemetry-instrumentation-genai-openai/tests/test_responses.py#L1462-L1497) and [`_AsyncErrorInjectingStreamDelegate`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python-genai/blob/main/instrumentation/opentelemetry-instrumentation-genai-anthropic/tests/test_async_messages.py#L725-L802). Add a `raise` inside the `with` block for the caller-side case.

Mocks are still fine for a stream that ends without a completion event.

replies.body: Done in 0e010416. When accumulation or rebuild fails, the stream now clears the output messages after recording the interaction, so `gen_ai.output.messages` stays unset instead of holding an empty text part. Both failure tests now assert the attribute is absent, and I added the same check for a rebuild error on the `fetch` stream.

replies.body: Done in cf0a235a. Streamed messages no longer set `finish_reason`, and `create` now passes `finish_reason=None`, the same as `fetch` on main, so the value lives only in `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons`. One visible change: a non-streamed `create` message now has `"finish_reason": null` where main reports `"stop"`. I updated the tests that asserted the old value.
